summary: Cap Haitien International Airport (CAP) serves Cap-Haïtien, the second-largest city in Haiti and the historic capital of the Kingdom of Haiti under King Henri Christophe. Located on the country's northern Caribbean coast, the airport is the primary gateway to the UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Citadelle Laferrière and the Sans-Souci Palace. It has undergone modernization efforts to support growing tourism in northern Haiti.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Cap Haitien International Airport?
A: The airport is served by several carriers including American Airlines, Spirit Airlines, and regional carriers offering flights primarily from Miami, Fort Lauderdale, and Port-au-Prince.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Cap-Haïtien?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers east of the city center, typically a 10–15 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Are there direct international flights to Cap Haitien?
A: Yes, there are direct international flights from a few US cities, primarily in Florida, with seasonal and charter additions.

Q: Can I visit the Citadelle Laferrière from this airport?
A: Absolutely. Cap Haitien is the standard departure point for excursions to the Citadelle and Sans-Souci Palace, located in the mountains south of the city.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared transportation (tap-taps) are available outside the terminal and are the primary means of getting to and from the airport. Negotiate fares in advance, as metered taxis are uncommon. Rental cars can be arranged but driving in Haiti requires local familiarity and caution.
local_tip: Pack light and keep your passport and valuables on you at all times—baggage handling can be informal, and having essentials in a carry-on makes your onward journey to the Citadelle or local hotels much smoother.
